Let me analyze this certificate.

Certificate number: R60/2000-NL1-09.08
Scheme: This is under the OIML Basic Certificate System for Measuring Instruments... Actually R60 certificates under the "OIML Certificate System for Load Cells" — scheme A or B? The certificate mentions "Issuing Authority" and conformity assessment. The OIML-CS has scheme A and B. R60/2000-NL1-09.08 - issued 2009, before OIML-CS merger, under the OIML Certificate System for Load Cells (which required both type evaluation). Typically we'd classify scheme... The cert says "Test Report" — the load cell system is essentially Scheme A (test report required)? Hmm. In OIML-CS, Scheme A = certificate without test report being part? Actually:

- Scheme A: the OIML certificate is issued on the basis of... the issuing authority issues the certificate and test report together? Let me recall: OIML CS Scheme A: "The applicant submits application with documentation to an issuing authority... The issuing authority... issues the OIML certificate and OIML type evaluation report." Scheme B: "issued on the basis of a test report from another body..." Actually:

Scheme A: Issuing Authority both evaluates (or reviews) the documentation and issues certificate + test report (TE report included). Scheme B: The applicant obtains a test report from... no wait.

From OIML-CS: 
- Scheme A: The OIML certificate and the OIML type evaluation report are issued together by the issuing authority. 
- Scheme B: The OIML certificate alone... "Scheme B applies when a test report... is issued by a different entity"? 

Actually per OIML-CS documents: Scheme A involves issuance of certificate together with type evaluation report; Scheme B involves issuance of a certificate without a type evaluation report (the report is held by manufacturer? no...). Hmm.

OIML-CS (2017) has two schemes: Scheme A — certificate + test report issued by issuing authority (recommended/recommended when...?), Scheme B — certificate only, where the test report is not part of the OIML CS documents delivered to participants? Actually Scheme B: "the OIML certificate is issued together with a test report which... the test report may be issued by a party different from the issuing authority."

Given ambiguity, safer: This 2009 certificate is under the old system. The certificate explicitly says "This Certificate attests the conformity ... (represented by the sample or samples identified in the associated Test Report, the test certificate and the description with number TC7579 ...)". There's a test report R60/2000-NL1-09.08 with 54 pages.

For scheme, given the presence of an associated test report issued with the certificate, I'd say scheme "A"? Hmm, many extractors put scheme: "A" for load cell certificates where the report is included. Actually in OIML-CS Scheme A, the certificate is issued "on the basis of a type evaluation" — test report forms part. Scheme B is for certificates issued without a full type evaluation report (e.g., based on manufacturer's tests?). Hmm.

Let me just recall: OIML CS brochure: "Scheme A: ... issuing authority ... reviews the evaluation results... issues the OIML type evaluation report and OIML certificate." "Scheme B: ... the applicant has a test report... submitted to the issuing authority, which issues the OIML certificate only." Under scheme B, the certificate alone is issued; the test report is issued separately (not by the issuing authority? or is not "OIML type evaluation report"?).

Given NMi Certin issued both certificate and test report (test report N° R60/2000-NL1-09.08, same number), scheme A seems right. I'll go with "A".
